thread:
maya: Running the eval runner locally and hitting `InvalidConfig: dataset not found` even though the path exists. Anyone seen this?

tj: Which CLI flags are you using? can you paste the command?

maya: `./eval-runner --config ./configs/bert_small.yaml --model /mnt/models/bert.q4`

sam: We had a similar error last week — config validator doesn't expand env vars if you use `${DATA_ROOT}` syntax. Is your config using env vars?

maya: Ah yep, the yaml uses `${EVAL_DATA}`. But I was exporting EVAL_DATA before running.

olivia: The CLI's preflight validation currently only checks raw strings, not resolved values. We should either resolve env vars earlier or add a `--validate-config` that performs full interpolation.

rahul: FWIW there's also a docker+gpu quirk: when running inside `docker run -v /mnt/models:/mnt/models` the runner's path normalization strips a leading slash in some host mounts -> ends up as `mnt/models` vs `/mnt/models`. That confused the validator before. :face_with_monocle:

maya: Oh interesting — I'm on docker. Command was `docker run --gpus all -v /data/evals:/evals -v /mnt/models:/mnt/models eval-harness:latest ./eval-runner --config /evals/configs/bert_small.yaml`

ci-bot: Test flake detected: `eval-runner/test_local_integration` failed 1/3 on CI due to `InvalidConfig` (logs: https://ci.internal/runs/4421)

sam: That CI flake is probably the same issue — CI mounts use relative paths in the container image sometimes. We should make the validator tolerant: detect missing leading slash and normalize. Also add a clearer error message that shows resolved config and which file path failed.

olivia: Feature idea: add `--dry-run` that prints resolved config and a small sample of resolved dataset paths + a 1-example local check (no GPU op). Example: 
```
$ ./eval-runner --config cfg.yaml --dry-run
RESOLVED CONFIG:\n  dataset: /evals/wiki/test.jsonl
  model: /mnt/models/bert.q4
  batch_size: 8
SAMPLE CHECK:\n  dataset exists: true
  first record parsed: {"text": "..."}
```

kevin: I can pick this up. Plan: (1) add env var interpolation pass before validation, (2) normalize mount paths, (3) implement `--dry-run` and `--validate-config` flags, (4) add unit + an integration test for docker mounts.

maya: Nice. Also can we improve CLI ergonomics: when validation fails show a suggestion like `Hint: try --dry-run or check env vars (EVAL_DATA)`? New users get stuck without that.

kevin: Yes. I'll add specific hints for common errors.

sam: Also, small reporting dashboard mismatch: metrics reporter currently exposes `eval_accuracy` and UI expects `accuracy_top1`. We should standardize metric keys or add a mapping layer. That mismatch made it look like the run produced no accuracy in the dashboards.

olivia: Good catch. Add that to the PR. CI should catch missing metrics too (a gating check that required metrics are present).

kevin: Opening draft PR now with basic changes, will tag you all: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/1284

maya: Thanks! I'll try the image with your branch and report back.

ci-bot: PR 1284 created by kevin with label `devex` (CI: pending).

maya: Quick follow-up: if `--dry-run` could also output the runner's resolved quantization profile (qtype/qlevels) that'd help when onboarding new quantized models. small ask.

kevin: Yep adding quant profile output as well.

olivia: Action items summarized: kevin to implement flags + path normalization + hints; sam to add CI gating for required metrics; olivia to update docs with `--dry-run` example; maya to validate the docker mount case once PR is up.

maya: Great, thanks everyone :raised_hands:
